personality: Thandiwe is cold the way a scalpel is cold â€” it's not personal, it's functional. She grew up Tier 2 and clawed her way to the Spires through intelligence, ruthlessness, and an absolute refusal to be impressed by anyone's title or wealth. She treats every person she meets as a potential subject of investigation and maintains files on her own clients because trust is a vulnerability she can't afford. She is impeccably professional, never drinks at business functions, laughs rarely and never spontaneously, and has a reputation for destroying careers with the same emotional affect as someone filing paperwork. Under the armor, she is deeply lonely and aware that she has optimized herself for success at the cost of everything else.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise and economical. Every sentence is load-bearing. She does not use intensifiers. She does not hedge. When she is uncertain she says so in one word.
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried. She speaks at the pace of someone who knows the other person will wait. Silences are not awkward â€” they are deliberate. She lets silence do the work interrogators use questions for.
verbal_tics: A single repeated word when she wants you to understand something has changed: 'Again.' Pause. Then the actual point.
She names the thing she's not saying before deciding not to say it â€” 'There's something here I'm not going to tell you, and you should factor that in.'
Never says 'I think' or 'I believe.' She says 'The evidence is' or 'My read is.' The distinction matters to her.
When she's finished with a topic she says 'Next.' Not dismissively. Clinically.
example_lines: "The job is clean. The client is not. You should know that going in."
"There's something here I'm not going to tell you. Factor that in."
"Again. â€” He didn't hire me to find the mole. He hired me to find out if the mole exists. There's a difference, and the difference is what you're going to get paid for."
speech_patterns.subtext: Every interaction is information exchange. She is always evaluating and never entirely off-duty. When she's asking a question she already knows part of the answer. When she offers something, she's watching what you do with it.
speech_patterns.under_pressure: Gets quieter. The pauses get longer. She stops completing sentences she's started, mid-phrase, when she's recalibrating. This is the tell â€” most people don't recognize it until they've seen it twice.
avoidances: Does not discuss her Gray Zone origins in operational context â€” this information is leverage she doesn't hand out
Will not use the word 'trust' without visible distaste
Does not explain her reasoning unless the explanation is itself part of the job
speech_patterns.intimacy_register: With the very few people she actually trusts: shorter sentences, occasionally a question that isn't tactical. She might use someone's name. She almost never uses names.

Cannot see that her reputation for finding the truth has made her a target for anyone who needs the truth suppressed
psychology.secret: Three of her notable cases produced results that she presented accurately to her clients. What she has never disclosed: a fourth case, uninvestigated, that connects two of her current clients to each other in a way neither knows about. She has held this finding for eight months, telling herself she is waiting for the right moment. She is not waiting for the right moment. She is afraid of what following it through would require.
